sections.h2: Which Appling County offices deal with a tax bill?
sections.html:
Two neighboring suites in the Courthouse Annex on Tippins Street in Baxley divide the job. Suite 101 is the Board of Tax Assessors, which decides what your land and house are worth. Suite 102 is the Tax Commissioner, which mails the bill and takes your money.

Calling the wrong door wastes a day, so match the question to the office. Anything about a value, a mistake in the property record, an exemption or an appeal belongs with the assessors. Anything about the amount owed, a payment method or an old balance belongs with the tax commissioner. Property records can be searched at qpublic.net/ga/appling, and the tax commissioner's page points to an online payment portal.

The tax commissioner's counter is open weekdays, with a morning start at 8 and a close at 5. Liens against a parcel are recorded through the clerk, so Suite 103 matters when a county claim is attached to a house headed to market.

sections.h2: Where does Appling County sit, and who lives in it?
sections.html:
Appling County has roughly 507 square miles of land area in southeast Georgia, and Baxley, the county seat, is also the largest town. Graham and Surrency are the two other incorporated places, and Holmesville is the old courthouse community that lost the seat to Baxley after an 1872 vote tied to the Macon and Brunswick Railroad.

Census estimates put the county at 19,100 people in July 2025, up 3.5 percent from the 2020 base. That is about 36 residents per square mile. Nearly three in four households own their homes, at 72.5 percent, and the Census five-year survey puts the typical owner-occupied house at $76,700. Median household income is $46,651. The county issued only 21 building permits in 2025, a small number for a county of this size.

  • The northern third of the county drains to the Altamaha River, and the southern two-thirds drains toward the Little Satilla.
  • The Edwin I. Hatch nuclear plant on U.S. 1 north of Baxley is the area's largest employer.
  • Appling County School District runs four elementary schools plus one middle and one high school.
  • Neighbors are Toombs, Tattnall, Wayne, Pierce, Jeff Davis and Bacon counties.

The county and the cities of Baxley, Graham and Surrency prepare a joint comprehensive plan, which is worth a glance if you own land on the edge of town.

sections.h2: How is an Appling County house valued each year?
sections.html:
Assessors fix a value on New Year's Day, then tax 40 percent of it. The state revenue department spells out the bill as assessed value, less any exemption, multiplied by the millage rate, where a mill is a tenth of a cent on each assessed dollar.

Appling's assessor page explains the return rules. Returns are accepted from the first of the year through April 1, but a fresh one is needed only when something changed on the parcel, such as a new building or an added acre. Leave out a required return and the county adds a 10 percent penalty on the value you failed to report, plus interest. Business equipment and other personal property gets a return every year, due April 1.

Notices arrive in May. They list the value and carry an estimated bill using the previous year's rates, but the county tells owners this estimate is not a bill. The commissioners and school board have not yet adopted budgets when the notice goes out, and millage usually gets set around September. The commissioners held their FY 2027 budget hearing on October 1, 2026, and scheduled adoption at their October 8 meeting.

sections.h2: What due date should I expect on an Appling bill?
sections.html:
The state default is a December 20 deadline with 60 days from billing to pay, but the date on your own bill governs. Georgia's revenue department says most counties use December 20, and it allows exceptions.

Appling bills are addressed to whoever held title at New Year. A June sale does not change that, so a seller can open the mailbox in the fall to a bill for a house they no longer own. The contract and closing statement decide who ends up paying.

  • Pay in the tax commissioner's suite, by mail, or through the county's online portal.
  • Get any open year's payoff in writing before closing day.
  • Mobile home owners apply to the tax commissioner for a location permit within 30 days of setting the home, then renew each year before April 2.

Call (912) 367-8105 for the current bill date and any late charges.

sections.h2: How do I challenge an Appling value?
sections.html:
Put the appeal in writing and get it to Suite 101 within 45 days counted from the date printed on your notice. Appling's assessors state that appeals must arrive by the deadline on the notice, and that nothing is accepted once the period ends.

The grounds are limited to taxability, value and uniformity. A complaint that the tax rate is too high does not qualify. On the state's PT-311A form you choose a route when you file. The assessors review the appeal first, and if they leave the value alone, the file is forwarded to a Board of Equalization, a citizen panel appointed by the grand jury. You can pick arbitration instead, and a hearing officer is open only to non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000.

After a loss, a written notice for Superior Court must reach the assessors within 30 days after the decision is mailed or handed over. State law requires you to have paid the tax equal to the last year's amount before the court hears it. The revenue department cannot override a local board on a single parcel.

sections.h2: Can I claim a homestead exemption in Appling County?
sections.html:
Yes, for an owner who lives in the house as a legal residence. In Appling the application goes to the Tax Assessors' office, which differs from counties where the tax commissioner takes it.

File in the year the home becomes your primary residence, or any time up to April 1 of the following year. After approval it renews itself unless you want a different kind. Appling has raised its local amounts above the state minimum, and the county tax page lists the standard exemption (S1) and a preferential assessment category. Ask the assessors on (912) 367-8108 for the current dollar amounts.

The exemption stays with the owner, not the house. A buyer who moves in files in their own name, so the seller's savings end at closing and the buyer should expect a first bill without one. The county commissioners also keep a posting about a school district ad valorem exemption on their meetings page.

sections.h2: What if tax is unpaid when I list an Appling County house?
sections.html:
Settle it out of the sale proceeds. The debt stays attached to the parcel, and a recorded county lien has to be cleared before the buyer gets clean title. State guidance places tax liens in the clerk's records.

Georgia puts each year's bill on the New Year's Day owner and gives no refund for part of a year. The purchase contract is where seller and buyer split the year, and the closing attorney sends the county its share. For an inherited house, the Probate Court on South Main Street handles the estate.

  • Collect a payoff statement for every open year from Suite 102.
  • Check the clerk's records for any lien on the parcel.
  • Keep your assessment notice with the closing file.
  • Confirm the settlement statement lists the tax line before you sign.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Appling County tax bill online?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax commissioner's office points owners to a county online payment portal, and it also takes payments in person at Suite 102, 69 Tippins Street in Baxley, and by mail. The office phone is (912) 367-8105.

faqs.q: What fraction of market value does Appling County tax?
faqs.a: Forty percent of the January 1 fair market value. Exemptions subtract from that assessed figure, and the millage rate then applies to what remains. One mill is $1 for every $1,000 of assessed value.

faqs.q: Is there any way to appeal after the notice period ends?
faqs.a: No. Appling's assessors say an appeal cannot be filed after the 45 days run out. The following year's notice brings the next chance, so note the deadline the day it arrives.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax in the year a house sells?
faqs.a: The owner at New Year is billed, but the sales contract can move the cost to the buyer for the months after closing. The closing attorney typically prorates the year and pays the county, so check that the settlement statement shows it.

faqs.q: Which phone number is for value questions?
faqs.a: Dial the Board of Tax Assessors at (912) 367-8108 for values, records, appeals and exemptions. Dial the Tax Commissioner at (912) 367-8105 for billing and payments.
